result.reason: All 3 immutable criteria MET, verified independently rather than inherited. NOTE FIRST: this was CYCLE 2, not cycle 1 — a cycle-1 FAIL already existed on disk (13:25) and Main had fixed it; measured mtimes (critique 13:25 < tests 13:30 < log_redaction.py 13:38 < experiment_results 13:39) show evidence changed after the FAIL, so this is the documented changed-evidence flow, not verdict-shopping. I appended rather than overwrote, so the cycle-1 FAIL is preserved. The cycle-1 blocker is genuinely repaired: I reproduced the exact leak scenario myself — a fresh subprocess in the losing order checked in at scripts/migrations/extend_historical_data.py:39-41, issuing a REAL requests.get against a REAL local socket so urllib3.connectionpool emits a genuine record, plus the backend.tools.fred_data exception re-emission channel — and measured LEAKED_CREDENTIAL=False with URL_WAS_LOGGED=True and REDACTION_MARKER_PRESENT=True, so the result is provably non-vacuous. My own mutant MU-Q1 (neuter _install_addhandler_hook before collection, reconstructing the cycle-1 design) kills 11 tests, so the suite is sensitive to the cycle-1 blocker. Deterministic gates: immutable command exit=0 / 45 passed; secret_leak_regression exit=0; full backend suite 31 failed / 2471 passed, and a control with 82.7 neutered re-running those exact 31 node-ids leaves all 31 still failing (symmetric difference empty -> ZERO regressions introduced by a process-wide addHandler monkeypatch) while test_phase_75_sre_ops::test_c6_redaction_survives_json_branch flips fail->pass, confirming 82.7 repairs a previously-red redaction test. My independent 9th-site sweep used two query shapes neither Main nor the researcher used and found NO ninth URL-query-string leak site; the hook-bypass hunt found no production propagate=False, no dictConfig/fileConfig, and both basicConfig(handlers=[...]) sites route through root.addHandler so the hook covers them. Harness compliance clean: LOG-LAST respected (0 'phase=82.7' entries in harness_log.md, masterplan status still pending), all 3 criteria verbatim in the contract, researcher before contract. Research-gate envelope irregularity judged ACCEPTABLE on independent review. FOUR WARN / FIVE NOTE findings recorded, none criterion-violating. No real credential VALUE appears in any artifact. OPERATOR ACTION STILL OWED: rotate FRED_API_KEY — this step closes the logging channel, it does not un-disclose the already-leaked value.
result.notes:
WARN-1 (qa.md 4c shape #11, mis-attributed kill mechanism): backend/tests/test_phase_82_7_credential_logging.py:176 test_descendant_loggers_are_covered_not_just_the_named_parents carries the docstring "THE CYCLE-1 BLOCKER, pinned" but SURVIVED my MU-Q1 — it is absent from the 11 failures. Cause: the `capture` fixture attaches its handler to root BEFORE the test body calls install_secret_redaction(), so the plain HANDLER leg (which existed in cycle 1 and in phase-60.4) scrubs the record; the test cannot distinguish the cycle-1 design from the cycle-2 design. The blocker IS genuinely pinned, by test_install_survives_a_later_basicConfig and test_a_handler_added_after_install_is_filtered, so this is a vacuous guard alongside two genuine behavioural ones — WARN, not blocking, per qa.md 4c verdict wiring. Named fix: attach the capture handler AFTER install (or assert h.filters == []) so the test observes the leg it names.
WARN-2 (proxy assertion): 8 of my 11 MU-Q1 kills come from test_every_swept_site_installs_redaction_at_import, which asserts the module-state flag lr._HOOK_INSTALLED rather than an absence-of-credential behaviour. Adequate in combination, but criterion 3's per-site breadth leans on a state flag.
WARN-3 (carried from cycle 1, unchanged): backend/services/observability/log_redaction.py:75-76 and :159-161 are both bare `except Exception: pass` on a SECURITY filter — by construction they cannot fail loudly, which is the exact mechanism that hid Main's first type(exc)(cleaned) attempt. A counter or logging.raiseExceptions-style breadcrumb would make a future regression visible.
WARN-4 (evaluator self-catch, methodology): my own first bypass sweep used unquoted --include=*.py, which zsh glob-expanded so grep returned "no matches" for every shape — a false CLEAN, vacuity shape #9 reproducing on the evaluator. All sweeps were re-run quoted; anyone re-running these gates on this machine must quote the include pattern.
NOTE-1: ruff exit=1 on one F401, `backend.econ_calendar.registry.CalendarSource imported but unused` at backend/econ_calendar/sources/finnhub_earnings.py:26. I proved pre-existence independently rather than inheriting cycle 1's proof — extracted the HEAD blob via `git show HEAD:...` and linted it in isolation, same "Found 1 error". The 82.7 hunk on that file adds only the redaction import + call near line 28 and does not touch line 26. Gate scope is what the CHANGE defines, so NOTE not blocker — but it sits two lines from a hunk this step added and is a one-token cleanup.
NOTE-2: Main's mutation-matrix row "MU6 addHandler hook removed -> 10 failed" vs my independent MU-Q1 -> 11 failed. Not a contradiction (different mutant shapes; mine also stops _HOOK_INSTALLED ever flipping), but the row should name the mutant precisely.
NOTE-3 (measured latent gap, NOT a live leak): _SECRET_PARAM_RE's alternation omits bare `key` and `password` — measured `?key=<32ch>` redacted=False, `?password=<32ch>` redacted=False, while api_key/apikey/api-key/token/X-Api-Key all redact True. I then swept backend/ scripts/ functions/ for `[?&](key|apiKey|password|passwd|pwd|sig|signature)=` and got ZERO hits, so there is no current exposure. Recommend queueing onto the existing 82.32.
NOTE-4: the researcher's structured return dropped, which is now the second such drop this session. The transport defect is worth its own queued step; the gate itself is fine (brief on disk, envelope complete as its final section, gate_passed true, and the gate demonstrably worked — it caught the 8th site fx_rates.py that Main's own grep missed).
NOTE-5: masterplan `82.7 retry_count` is still 0 despite a genuine cycle-1 FAIL. The F1 discipline uses that counter for certified_fallback escalation, so leaving it at 0 understates consecutive fails. Bookkeeping only.
SPAWN-PROMPT DRIFT: my spawn prompt described cycle-1 state ("32 passed", a fix with no addHandler hook, "create the critique file") and listed attacks A-E against the cycle-1 design. All of that was stale. I evaluated the CURRENT tree, not the prompt's description of it. Attack A/B/C/D/E were all still run, but re-aimed at the cycle-2 design.
CREDENTIAL HYGIENE: no credential VALUE appears in the critique file or in this return; keys named by ENV VAR NAME only. I did not read backend/.env and did not grep any log for a key value. No real credential value was found in any artifact of this step.
VERDICT FILE: appended to handoff/current/evaluator_critique_82.7.md as a new "# CYCLE 2" section; the cycle-1 FAIL (sections 0-8 + its fenced json) is preserved byte-for-byte above it, and the file now opens with a pointer saying the LAST fenced json block is the verdict of record. This is the only file I wrote; all production code, tests and other handoff files were read-only.
